title: pvMaterialInterfaceFilter
body:
## pvMaterialInterfaceFilter

Finds material fragments in AMR (hierarchical box) data such as CTH Spy Plot output: cells whose material fraction exceeds MaterialFractionThreshold are connected into fragments, whose surfaces form output port 0 (geometry) and whose centres of mass, volumes, masses and selected weighted averages form a point set on port 1 (statistics). It can invert the fraction and clip with a plane or sphere to measure craters, and can write both outputs to text files. Use pvRectilinearGridConnectivity for rectilinear multiblock data.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Material fraction arrays are expected as unsigned char (the Spy Plot reader's down-conversion); float fractions are not offered for SelectMaterialFractionArrays.
- Mass arrays pair with fraction arrays by list position; keep both lists in the same order.
- WriteGeometryOutput and WriteStatisticsOutput write files outside Schemaxis-managed exports.
- Schemaxis serial examples do not establish MPI or client-server behaviour. Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `MaterialInterfaceFilter`. Identity: `filters/MaterialInterfaceFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: Input to the filter can be a hierarchical box data set containing image data or a multiblock of rectilinear grids. Accepted data: non-overlapping AMR data (vtkNonOverlappingAMR). The input needs at least one cell-centred array. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkNonOverlappingAMR"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType` | This property sets the type of clip geometry, and associated parameters. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["None","Plane","Sphere"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"None"}` |
| `ComputeOBB` | Compute Object Oriented Bounding boxes (OBB). When active the result of this computation is copied into the statistics output. In the case that the filter is built in its validation mode, the OBB's are rendered. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Computemassweightedaverageover` | For arrays selected a mass weighted average is computed. These arrays are also copied into fragment geometry cell data as the fragment surfaces are generated. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Computevolumeweightedaverageover` | For arrays selected a volume weighted average is computed. The values of these arrays are also copied into fragment geometry cell data as the fragment surfaces are generated. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `InvertVolumeFraction` | Inverting the volume fraction generates the negative of the material. It is useful for analyzing craters. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `MaterialFractionThreshold` | Material fraction is defined as normalized amount of material per voxel. Any voxel in the input data set with a material fraction greater than this value is included in the output data set. | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.08,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.08` |
| `OutputBaseName` | This property specifies the base including path of where to write the statistics and geometry output text files. It follows the pattern "/path/to/folder/and/file" here file has no extension, as the filter will generate a unique extension. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `SelectMassArrays` | Mass arrays are paired with material fraction arrays. This means that the first selected material fraction array is paired with the first selected mass array, and so on sequentially. As the filter identifies voxels meeting the minimum material fraction threshold, these voxel's mass will be used in fragment center of mass and mass calculation. A warning is generated if no mass array is selected for an individual material fraction array. However, in that case the filter will run without issue because the statistics output can be generated using fragments' centers computed from axis aligned bounding boxes. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `SelectMaterialFractionArrays` | Material fraction is defined as normalized amount of material per voxel. It is expected that arrays containing material fraction data has been down converted to a unsigned char. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `WriteGeometryOutput` | If this property is set, then the geometry output is written to a text file. The file name will be constructed using the path in the "Output Base Name" widget. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `WriteStatisticsOutput` | If this property is set, then the statistics output is written to a text file. The file name will be constructed using the path in the "Output Base Name" widget. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `ClipType` → `None`

Syntax: `{"type":"None","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/None`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

No authored options.


### Nested `ClipType` → `Plane`

Syntax: `{"type":"Plane","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Plane`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType.options.Normal` | Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Offset` | Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ClipType.options.Origin` | A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |

### Nested `ClipType` → `Sphere`

Syntax: `{"type":"Sphere","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `implicit_functions/Sphere`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClipType.options.Center` | Centre [x, y, z] of the sphere in the input’s coordinates; the region within Radius of this point is inside. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `ClipType.options.Radius` | Radius of the sphere: points closer than Radius to Center are inside. A larger radius encloses more of the data or moves the cut shell outward. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvMaterialInterfaceFilter",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
